Migrate this Next.js project from Pages Router to App Router. The project currently uses the pages directory structure with two pages (index and about). You need to:

1. Create the app directory with the proper App Router structure
2. Migrate the pages from pages/ to app/ (index → app/page.tsx, about → app/about/page.tsx)
3. Create a root layout file (app/layout.tsx) with proper HTML structure and shared metadata
4. Remove the pages directory and any pages-specific files
5. Update imports and routing patterns to use App Router conventions
6. Ensure the migrated app builds and runs correctly

Keep the same functionality and UI, but use App Router patterns and file structure.

Version 13 introduces the new [`next/font`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/font) module which gives you the ability to customize your font loading experience while still ensuring great performance and privacy. `next/font` is supported in both the `pages` and `app` directories. 118- 119-While [inlining CSS](/docs/app/api-reference/components/font) still works in `pages`, it does not work in `app`. You should use [`next/font`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/font) instead. 120- 121-See the [Font Optimization](/docs/app/api-reference/components/font) page to learn how to use `next/font`. 122- 123-## Migrating from `pages` to `app` 124- 125-> **🎥 Watch:** Learn how to incrementally adopt the App Router → [YouTube (16 minutes)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YQMSietiFm0). 126- 127-Moving to the App Router may be the first time using React features that Next.js builds on top of such as Server Components, Suspense, and more. events.content:
The project now uses the App Router. `next build` passes, and both routes are prerendered as static pages. I started the production server and fetched `/` and `/about`: each returns the same title, description, viewport tag, favicon link, heading and nav links as before.

**New files**
- **`app/layout.tsx`**: the root layout. It replaces `_app.tsx` and `_document.tsx`, renders `<html lang="en"><body>`, and holds the shared metadata:
  - a default title and description
  - the favicon (`icons: { icon: '/favicon.ico' }`)
  - a `viewport` export (`width: 'device-width', initialScale: 1`)
- **`app/page.tsx`**: the home page. Its `next/head` block became a `metadata` export with the title "Home Page" and the description.
- **`app/about/page.tsx`**: the about page, with the title "About Us" and its description.

**Removed:** the whole `pages/` directory (`_app.tsx`, `_document.tsx`, `index.tsx`, `about.tsx`).

**Routing:** the plain `<a href>` links are now `<Link>` from `next/link`, so navigation happens in the browser without a full page reload. The rendered HTML is the same.

**Small side effects:**
- Two pages behave slightly differently from before:
  - The favicon link used to be on the home page only; it's now on every page.
  - The viewport tag used to be set only on the home page. The new App Router adds it to every page anyway, so I declared it once in the layout.
- During the build, Next.js rewrote `tsconfig.json`. It added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include` and expanded the arrays onto multiple lines.
- I added `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts` to `.gitignore`, since the build generates both.

**Already broken before the migration:**
- The `/contact` link points to a page that doesn't exist, so it still goes to a 404.
- There is no `public/` folder, so `/favicon.ico` doesn't exist either.

Nothing has been committed.

cd /workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs; ls 01-app/02-guides/migrating; sed -n 1,400p 01-app/02-guides/migrating/app-router-migration.md 2>/dev/null | grep -n -A30 -i "Root Layout\|next/head\|metadata\|viewport" | head -200

cd /workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs; grep -n -B2 -A25 "^## Viewport\|viewport\b" 01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/generate-viewport.md | head -60; grep -n -A15 "^### .icons" 01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/generate-metadata.md | head -30
cd /workspace && git rm -rq pages && npm run build 2>&1 | tail -25

(npx next start -p 3123 >/tmp/next.log 2>&1 &) ; sleep 4; for p in / /about; do echo "== $p"; curl -s localhost:3123$p | grep -oE ']*>|[^<]*|]*>|]*>|

[^<]*
